Engine components and the Android runtime payload.

godot_editor_component and godot_runtime_component declare the editor or the runtime of one
slot and its toolchain registration; godot_android_runtime combines the Android shell
library with the engine library into an Android runtime payload. See
[engines](../../engine.md).

<a id="godot_android_runtime"></a>

## godot_android_runtime

<pre>
load("@rules_godot//godot/engine:defs.bzl", "godot_android_runtime")

godot_android_runtime(<a href="#godot_android_runtime-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_android_runtime-shell">shell</a>, <a href="#godot_android_runtime-engine_library">engine_library</a>, <a href="#godot_android_runtime-kwargs">**kwargs</a>)
</pre>

Join Godot's Android shell library with an engine library into one aar_import runtime.

`shell` is an Android shell AAR file, such as the one of an official release or the
AAR of a source-built shell library. Without `engine_library`, the shell's own JNI
libraries are used. With it, the shell AAR is repacked in the configuration of each
platform slice, as the engine AAR, with that platform slice's engine library as
`jni/<abi>/libgodot_android.so`; the ABI follows the CPU of the platform slice, so
one target per variant serves every CPU, and `engine_library` may be a select()
over the CPU. Delivery copies are stripped as Bazel's `--strip` asks; the
`<name>.debug_symbols` of applications with this runtime contain them unstripped.
The ruleset supplies the shell library's Maven dependencies. Use the result as the
payload of a godot_runtime_component for an Android slot. This macro returns no
value.

Example:
```starlark
godot_android_runtime(
    name = "android_release",
    shell = "@godot_android_shell//:release.aar",
    engine_library = "@godot_android_arm64_release//:libgodot_android.so",
)
```

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| files | many | always | build imported AAR metadata and engine libraries; no run behavior |

### Output groups
none

### Generated targets
none

### Providers
none


**PARAMETERS**


| Name  | Description | Default Value |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_android_runtime-name"></a>name |  Public aar_import target name.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_android_runtime-shell"></a>shell |  Godot's Android shell .aar file.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_android_runtime-engine_library"></a>engine_library |  Optional engine library .so target of the current platform slice.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_android_runtime-kwargs"></a>kwargs |  Remaining aar_import attributes, such as tags and visibility.   |  none |


<a id="godot_editor_component"></a>

## godot_editor_component

<pre>
load("@rules_godot//godot/engine:defs.bzl", "godot_editor_component")

godot_editor_component(*, <a href="#godot_editor_component-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-cpu">cpu</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-editor">editor</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-engine">engine</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-origin">origin</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-platform">platform</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-tags">tags</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-version">version</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_component-visibility">visibility</a>)
</pre>

Declare one execution-platform editor slot and its toolchain registration.

Creates the provenance-carrying toolchain implementation `<name>` and Bazel's
built-in `toolchain()` `<name>.toolchain`, constrained to the operating system and CPU
of the execution platform and to the engine selected by `--@rules_godot//godot:engine`.
A registration set is a package of components: register it with its `:all` pattern;
the first registered candidate of the selected engine for a slot wins. The
editor may be an executable target, such as a prebuilt editor archive's `:editor` or
a source recipe's `:godot`, or another editor component, whose payload and provenance
are forwarded.

Example:
```starlark
godot_editor_component(
    name = "editor_macos_arm64",
    editor = "@godot_editor_macos//:editor",
    platform = "macos",
    cpu = "arm64",
    version = "4.7.2",
)
```

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| files | many | always | build the editor payload and its runfiles; no run behavior |

### Output groups
none

### Generated targets
| name | kind | purpose | reason | visibility | testonly | prerequisites | availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {name}.toolchain | metadata | analysis_boundary | register the slot with editor_toolchain_type; toolchain resolution is a separate boundary | caller | inherit | none | always |
| {name}.engine | metadata | analysis_boundary | the config_setting on --@rules_godot//godot:engine that the toolchain requires for a named engine | caller | inherit | none | engine named |

### Providers
| name | role | availability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ToolchainInfo | godot editor files, executable, version and provenance | always |
| GodotComponentInfo | Provenance of the declared slot | always |

<a id="godot_runtime_component"></a>

## godot_runtime_component

<pre>
load("@rules_godot//godot/engine:defs.bzl", "godot_runtime_component")

godot_runtime_component(*, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-cpu">cpu</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-digest">digest</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-engine">engine</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-environment">environment</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-origin">origin</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-platform">platform</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-runtime">runtime</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-tags">tags</a>,
                        <a href="#godot_runtime_component-variant">variant</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-version">version</a>, <a href="#godot_runtime_component-visibility">visibility</a>)
</pre>

Declare one target-platform runtime slot and its toolchain registration.

Creates the provenance-carrying toolchain implementation `<name>` and Bazel's
built-in `toolchain()` `<name>.toolchain`, constrained to the target platform's operating
system, CPU and iOS environment, with `target_settings` on
`--@rules_godot//godot:variant` for the template variant and on
`--@rules_godot//godot:engine` for the engine. The runtime may be a
desktop template file, a target with GodotRuntimeInfo, an iOS XCFramework import or
`:engine_library`, an Android runtime, a `select()` between prepared same-slot
payloads, or another runtime component, whose payload and provenance are forwarded.
Every selected branch must fill the declared slot; slot facts are not configurable.

Example:
```starlark
godot_runtime_component(
    name = "runtime_ios_arm64_simulator_debug",
    runtime = "@godot_ios_arm64_simulator_debug//:engine_library",
    platform = "ios",
    cpu = "arm64",
    environment = "simulator",
    variant = "debug",
    version = "4.7.2",
)
```

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| files | many | always | build the runtime payload; no run behavior |

### Output groups
none

### Generated targets
| name | kind | purpose | reason | visibility | testonly | prerequisites | availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {name}.toolchain | metadata | analysis_boundary | register the slot with runtime_toolchain_type; toolchain resolution is a separate boundary | caller | inherit | none | always |
| {name}.engine | metadata | analysis_boundary | the config_setting on --@rules_godot//godot:engine that the toolchain requires for a named engine | caller | inherit | none | engine named |

### Providers
| name | role | availability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ToolchainInfo | godot runtime payload, GodotRuntimeInfo where known, version and provenance | always |
| GodotComponentInfo | Provenance of the declared slot | always |
